Dusk in an abandoned stepwell near Patan, Gujarat, no one else for miles. Jhanvi (30s), a heritage surveyor, descends the carved steps with a measuring tape and a torch, counting aloud to log the levels. At the fourth level she hears a second voice counting a half-beat behind her, from deep below. She stops; the counting stops one number later. She turns the torch down the shaft: only still green water. She climbs, counting under her breath, and the voice below counts with her, now closer than her own footsteps. At the top she steps into the open air and shuts the torch off; from the dark stepwell, a calm voice says the next number.
